sentences.zh: 一个是为联邦作战的黑人士兵，因为看过电影《光荣战役》的人都知道，这既是一个充满争议、同时又非常励志的故事。

sentences.en: One is black soldiers who fight for the Union, because anyone who's seen the film Glory will know that this is at once a contentious, but also a very inspiring story.
sentences.zh: 然后第二个群体，我认为值得我们讨论的，其实正是

sentences.en: And then the second group I think it's worth us talking about is actually the people who
sentences.zh: 这场战争所真正关乎的人，也就是南方联盟中的奴隶，那些被奴役的人民。

sentences.en: really are who the war is about, who are the slaves, the enslaved people in the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 那么联邦从一开始就有黑人士兵吗？

sentences.en: So do the Union have black soldiers right from the beginning?
sentences.zh: 不对，是这样的吗？

sentences.en: No, that's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不，他们没有。

sentences.en: No, they don't.
sentences.zh: 《解放宣言》所做的事情之一，就是为黑人部队的征召铺平了道路。

sentences.en: One of the things the Emancipation Proclamation does is to pave the way for the enlistment of black troops.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想有18.6万名黑人男子参军加入了联邦军队，另有1.5万到

sentences.en: And in the end, I think 186,000 black men enlist in the Union army and another 15 or
sentences.zh: 2万人加入了联邦海军。

sentences.en: 20,000 in the Union navy.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅从人数上看，他们就为联邦的胜利做出了极其重要的贡献，这还不算他们服役的意识形态和政治重要性。

sentences.en: And so make a hugely important contribution to Union victory in numbers terms alone, in addition to the ideological and political importance of their service.
sentences.zh: 但他们是在隔离的部队中作战。

sentences.en: But they're fighting segregated units.
sentences.zh: 他们不允许混编。

sentences.en: They're not allowed to mix.
sentences.zh: 他们的薪水更少，对吧？

sentences.en: They're earning less pay, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 在几乎整个战争期间，他们的薪水确实都更少。

sentences.en: They are earning less pay throughout almost the whole of the war.
sentences.zh: 他们在隔离部队中作战，指挥官大多是白人，通常是废奴主义者。

sentences.en: They're fighting in segregated units and mostly officered by white men, often abolitionists.
sentences.zh: 还有一个巨大的问题，如果他们被俘会怎么样？

sentences.en: And a huge issue, what happens to them if they get captured?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个巨大的问题，因为武装黑人男子对一个蓄奴社会来说绝对是终极噩梦。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a huge issue because, of course, arming black men is the ultimate nightmare in a slave society.
sentences.zh: 因此，《解放宣言》对南方联盟构成了极大的威胁。

sentences.en: And so the Emancipation Proclamation is incredibly threatening to the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 但征召黑人部队则是终极的侮辱。

sentences.en: But the enlistment of black troops is the ultimate insult.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这不仅仅是一种侮辱。

sentences.en: In fact, it's more than just an insult.
sentences.zh: 它有可能彻底粉碎他们的全部理论，即奴隶制赖以建立的整个理论，也就是黑人是无能的。

sentences.en: It threatens to blow apart their whole theory, the whole theory on which slavery is based, which is that black men are incapable.
sentences.zh: 因此，南方联盟拒绝像对待白人士兵那样对待黑人士兵。

sentences.en: And so the Confederacy refused to treat black soldiers as they would treat white soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他们对待白人士兵也相当糟糕，对吧？

sentences.en: And they're treating white soldiers pretty badly, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们把他们关进集中营里，让他们挨饿等等。

sentences.en: I mean, they're kind of locking them up in concentration camps and starving them and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们把他们关在战俘营里，成千上万的人因营养不良而死。

sentences.en: They're putting them in prisoner of war camps in which thousands of them die from malnutrition.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 那他们对黑人战俘做了什么？

sentences.en: So what are they doing to the black prisoners?
sentences.zh: 他们通常对黑人士兵做的事，其中有一些骇人听闻的例子，也许最臭名昭著的就是1864年的皮洛堡大屠杀。

sentences.en: To what they're often doing to the black soldiers, and there are some horrific examples of this, perhaps the most notorious being the Fort Pillow Massacre in 1864.
sentences.zh: 当黑人士兵投降时，他们遭到枪杀，有时在被枪杀前还会遭受酷刑。

sentences.en: When black soldiers surrender, they're being shot and sometimes tortured before they're shot.
sentences.zh: 制造了那场皮洛堡大屠杀的人，剧透一下，他就是三K党的创始人内森·贝德福德·福雷斯特。
zh_words: 内森·贝德福德·福雷斯特

sentences.en: And the guy who does that Fort Pillow Massacre, just to anticipate, he is Nathan Bedford Forrest, who's the founder of Ku Klux Klan.
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 那么，内战中对黑人士兵的暴力行为与内战后南方准军事暴力之间，是否存在一种延续性？

sentences.en: So is there a continuity between the violence towards black soldiers in the Civil War
sentences.zh: 这基本上可以解释为什么美国黑人没有迎来他们原以为被承诺的自由新生？

sentences.en: and then the paramilitary violence after the Civil War in the South that basically is one of the explanations
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对有。

sentences.en: for why black Americans don't have this new birth of freedom that they think they've been promised?
sentences.zh: 奴隶制本质上是压迫整个种族的暴力制度。

sentences.en: Yes, definitely.
sentences.zh: 随着奴隶制的破裂和走向终结，其他形式的暴力也随之登场。

sentences.en: Slavery is inherently a violent system of oppressing an entire race of people.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制本质上是压迫整个种族的暴力系统。

sentences.en: As slavery fractures and comes to an end, other systems of violence come into play.
sentences.zh: 随着奴隶制的解体和终结，其他暴力系统开始发挥作用。

sentences.en: And this is evident not just in the South, but in the North, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅在南方明显，在北方也同样明显，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there are, in 1863, terrible riots in New York, prompted by the introduction of a draft there.
sentences.zh: 因为在1863年，纽约发生了可怕的暴动，起因是当地推行征兵制。

sentences.en: And that sees black people lynched for, what, three or four days, is it, of rioting in New York?
sentences.zh: 结果导致黑人在纽约遭到私刑暴行，持续了大概三四天，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, in July, 1863.
sentences.zh: 是的，在1863年7月。

sentences.en: So, yes, as you say, these are riots by people, and many of them are Irish immigrants, who don't want to be conscripted into the Union Army.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所说，这些是民众发起的暴动，其中许多人是爱尔兰移民，他们不想被强征入联邦军队。

sentences.en: But their targets include a coloured orphan asylum, as it's called.
sentences.zh: 但他们的目标包括一个所谓的有色人种孤儿院。

sentences.en: In other words, visible African-American properties and places and people in New York City are among the main targets of the rioting mob in New York.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，纽约市里那些显眼的非裔美国人财产、场所和人员，成为了纽约暴动暴徒的主要目标之一。

sentences.en: So there is a rise in anti-black violence across the North in 1863 and 1864.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1863年和1864年，整个北方的反黑人暴力事件有所增加。

sentences.en: And there's a sense in which that's being driven, as in that instance in New York,
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，正如纽约的那次事件一样，这种暴力是由这样一群人推动的：

sentences.en: by people who believe that they, white people, are being called upon to make sacrifices on behalf of black people.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己——也就是白人——被要求为黑人做出牺牲。

sentences.en: And that somehow the government is now, the Lincoln administration is somehow now privileging black people
sentences.zh: 他们觉得现在的政府，也就是林肯政府，现在居然在优待黑人，

sentences.en: and demanding sacrifices from poor whites in order to uplift black people.
sentences.zh: 并要求贫穷的白人做出牺牲，以此来提升黑人的地位。

sentences.en: And is that because Lincoln has changed the terms of the war, because of emancipation, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为，这是因为林肯由于废奴而改变了战争的性质吗？

sentences.en: Is that driving that?
sentences.zh: 是这个原因在推动吗？

sentences.en: Definitely, yes.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, Lincoln would say he hasn't really changed the terms of the war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，林肯会说他并没有真正改变战争的性质。

sentences.en: It's still a war to save the Union, but it's a war in which the only way to save the Union
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一场为了拯救联邦的战争，但在这场战争中，拯救联邦的唯一方法

sentences.en: is to pull out what he would have called, other people did as well, the taproot of the rebellion.
sentences.zh: 就是拔除他所说的——其他人也这么说过——叛乱的根本。

sentences.en: And the taproot of the rebellion is slavery.
sentences.zh: 而叛乱的根本就是奴隶制。

sentences.en: So you destroy slavery in order to save the Union.
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须摧毁奴隶制来拯救联邦。

sentences.en: And when you destroyed slavery, you then have the question of how to integrate what they called the freedmen, formerly enslaved people, into the Republic.
sentences.zh: 而当你摧毁了奴隶制之后，随之而来的问题就是：如何将他们所称的“自由人”（即此前被奴役的人）融入共和国之中。

sentences.en: And so the things are all interrelated.
sentences.zh: 所以这些事情都是相互关联的。

sentences.en: But certainly the perception was that he had totally changed the basis of the war and that therefore the contract on which they may have initially been willing to fight and die
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，人们普遍认为他彻底改变了战争的基础，因此林肯政府

sentences.en: had been broken by the Lincoln administration.
sentences.zh: 已经打破了他们最初愿意为其战斗和牺牲的契约。

sentences.en: But Adam, also conversely, can I just ask you, on that question of how freed slaves are to be integrated
sentences.zh: 但是，亚当，反过来说，关于如何将获得自由的奴隶融入共和国的架构中这个问题，

sentences.en: into the fabric of the Republic, presumably Americans have this very Roman idea of the citizen soldier and that in a way to fight is to become a citizen.
sentences.zh: 我想问你，美国人大概有着非常罗马式的“公民士兵”观念，在某种意义上，战斗就是成为公民。

sentences.en: Is that something that is kind of underlying the recruitment of black regiments and so on?
sentences.zh: 这是否正是黑人军团招募等现象背后的深层原因？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And so in July 1863, you see this juxtaposition of images.
sentences.zh: 所以在1863年7月，你会看到这样一组并置的画面。

sentences.en: So Irishmen, who are often drawn in cartoons as looking like apes, rioting in order to avoid fighting for their country, for the flag,
sentences.zh: 一方面，卡片漫画中经常把爱尔兰人画得像猿猴一样，他们暴动是为了逃避为国家、为国旗而战；

sentences.en: juxtaposed against African-American troops fighting in South Carolina, Fort Wagner and other places, literally dying for the flag in the uniform.
sentences.zh: 而与之形成对照的是，非裔美国士兵在南卡罗来纳州、瓦格纳堡及其他地方浴血奋战，身着军服，真正为国旗献出生命。

sentences.en: And so Republicans, supporters of the Lincoln administration, look at that juxtaposition and say,
sentences.zh: 因此，共和党人以及林肯政府的支持者看到这种并置时会说：

sentences.en: how are we going to build a stable post-war republic once we've suppressed this rebellion?
sentences.zh: 一旦我们平息了这场叛乱，我们要如何建立一个稳定的战后共和国？

sentences.en: Who are going to be loyal citizens of this republic?
sentences.zh: 谁将成为这个共和国的忠实公民？

sentences.en: It's going to be black men, especially those who fought in the Union Army.
sentences.zh: 那将是黑人，尤其是那些在联邦军队中战斗过的人。

sentences.en: And that's in terms what Lincoln says in his, what turns out to be his last public address before he's assassinated,
sentences.zh: 这正是林肯在他最后一次公开演讲中所表达的观点——后来证明这也是他遇刺前的最后一次公开演讲，

sentences.en: in which he says, those black men who fought in our armies should surely be given the vote.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中说，那些在我们的军队中战斗过的黑人，理应获得投票权。

sentences.en: That's the way his mind is thinking at that point.
sentences.zh: 这就是他当时的想法。

sentences.en: And he doesn't add, but I don't think this is at all what Lincoln would think.
sentences.zh: 而且他没有加上——但我认为林肯绝对不会这么想——

sentences.en: And rioting Irishmen should have the franchise taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 那些暴动的爱尔兰人应该被剥夺选举权。

sentences.en: But certainly there are other Republicans who go to that, come to that conclusion.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，其他一些共和党人确实得出了这样的结论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so this serves as a reminder that while the war is going on, so also electoral politics are carrying on.
sentences.zh: 因此，这提醒了我们：在战争进行的同时，选举政治也在继续。

sentences.en: And there is an election coming up, isn't there, in which Lincoln's future as president is at stake.
sentences.zh: 而且马上就要举行选举了，对吧？林肯作为总统的未来正处于危急关头。

sentences.en: And the prospect of Lincoln losing the presidency, is that really the Confederacy's last chance?
sentences.zh: 林肯失去总统宝座的可能性，难道真的是邦联的最后机会吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And does that in turn determine, because of Gone with the Wind, it's incredibly famous, the blaze of destruction launched by General Sherman through Georgia and into the Carolinas?
sentences.zh: 这反过来是否决定了——因为《乱世佳人》的关系，谢尔曼将军穿过佐治亚州进入卡罗来纳州所发起的毁灭之火极其著名——

sentences.en: Is he trying to kind of demonstrate that the Confederacy is doomed and thereby ensure that Lincoln will win re-election?
sentences.zh: 他是否在试图证明邦联已经注定灭亡，从而确保林肯能够赢得连任？

sentences.en: Or is that too crude an equation?
sentences.zh: 还是说这种等同过于粗暴了？

sentences.en: Atlanta falls at the very beginning of September 1864, and the election is in November, I think, and it falls to Sherman.
sentences.zh: 亚特兰大在1864年9月初陷落，选举好像是在11月，它是被谢尔曼攻陷的。

sentences.en: It's a very big strategic gain for the union.
sentences.zh: 这对联邦来说是一个巨大的战略收获。

sentences.en: It's a railroad hub.
sentences.zh: 它是一个铁路枢纽。

sentences.en: And furthermore, it's been under siege.
sentences.zh: 此外，它一直处于被围困状态。

sentences.en: There's been a kind of standoff at Atlanta for several weeks.
sentences.zh: 亚特兰大已经陷入了一种长达数周的僵局。

sentences.en: It had been unclear whether Sherman would be able to break through.
sentences.zh: 此前并不清楚谢尔曼是否能够突破防线。

sentences.en: So the fact that he does is a huge impetus behind Lincoln's re-election bid in 1864.
sentences.zh: 因此，他成功攻克亚特兰大，成为了1864年林肯竞选连任背后的一大强劲动力。

sentences.en: The real destruction wrought by Sherman's army is in the early months of 1865, or it's actually after the election.
sentences.zh: 谢尔曼军队造成的真正破坏发生在1865年的头几个月，也就是选举之后。

sentences.en: But the beginning of it, the origins of it, which is the fall of the Atlanta definitely, as you say,
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，这一切的开端和根源——也就是亚特兰大的陷落——

sentences.en: Tom sets the stage for Lincoln's victory and kind of takes some of the pressure off him.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这为林肯的胜利奠定了基础，并在某种程度上减轻了他的压力。

sentences.en: Because earlier, just a few weeks earlier, in August 1864, Lincoln's own political sources were telling him he was going to lose.
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前，就在短短几周前的1864年8月，林肯自己的政治消息源还告诉他他会输。

sentences.en: I mean, he was pretty sure he was going to lose.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他当时确信自己会输。

sentences.en: That's how it looked.
sentences.zh: 情况看起来就是那样。

sentences.en: And he's up against his own former general, right?
sentences.zh: 而且他的竞争对手正是他自己以前的将军，对吧？

sentences.en: George McClellan.
sentences.zh: 乔治·麦克莱伦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who's the Democrat candidate and who basically says, enough of the war.
sentences.zh: 他是民主党候选人，基本上主张“战争够了，是时候妥协了”。

sentences.en: It's time to settle.
sentences.zh: 民主党内部意见不一，麦克莱伦在这件事上也有些左右而言他，毕竟他曾是一名将军。

sentences.en: Democrats are internally divided in and McClellan kind of squirms around on this because after all, he's a general.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，麦克莱伦所代表的民主党竞选纲领承诺与南方达成停战协定，其目的是进行谈判，并宣称要实现“重新统一”，对吧？

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, the Democratic platform on which McClellan stands commits them to an armistice with a view to negotiation with the idea, they say, of reunion, right?
sentences.zh: 他们还没有达到“让犯错的姐妹们安宁离去”的那种观点。

sentences.en: Then they haven't come to the let the Erring sisters depart in peace point of view.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是在那样说。

sentences.en: They're not saying that.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然在说我们想要重新统一。

sentences.en: They're still saying we want reunion.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都是这么想的。

sentences.en: Almost all of them are.
sentences.zh: 但他们不知为何幻想着可以通过谈判而不是战争来达成这一点。

sentences.en: But they're somehow imagining that it can be done through negotiation rather than through war.
sentences.zh: 那么他们对解放奴隶的态度是什么？

sentences.en: And what's their attitude on the emancipation of slaves?
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一种令人发指的背叛和干扰，是适得其反的。

sentences.en: And that it's an appalling betrayal and a distraction, that it's counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 那么他们会推翻解放政策吗？

sentences.en: So would they have reversed it?
sentences.zh: 他们肯定会推翻的。

sentences.en: They certainly would have reversed it.
sentences.zh: 如果麦克莱伦获胜，有一点我们可以确定，那就是解放政策将不复存在。

sentences.en: If McClellan had won, the one thing we can be sure of is that the emancipation policy would have gone.
sentences.zh: 单就奴隶这个议题而言。

sentences.en: Just on the issue of slaves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们还没谈到过的一个群体就是奴隶，也就是邦联内部的那些人，黑人男女，将近四百万之多。

sentences.en: I mean, the one group we haven't yet talked about are the slaves, the people in the Confederacy, the black men and women, almost four million of them.
sentences.zh: 亚当，他们的经历是怎样的？

sentences.en: And what has their experience been like, Adam?
sentences.zh: 因为他们没有被邦联军队征召入伍。

sentences.en: Because they're not being called up by the Confederate armies.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然在土地上劳作。

sentences.en: They're still working on the land.
sentences.zh: 但据推测，他们长期生活在那种大体上充满压迫和恐怖暴力的环境中。

sentences.en: But presumably, the climate, well, all their lives, they have lived in this climate of oppressive, horrific violence, by and large.
sentences.zh: 这种环境在战争期间加剧了吗？

sentences.en: And has that intensified during the war?
sentences.zh: 他们的生活变得更糟了吗？

sentences.en: Are their lives much worse?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们中的许多人已经逃亡了？

sentences.en: Or have many of them fled?
sentences.zh: 或者他们中有些人支持南方？

sentences.en: Or do they support the South, some of them?
sentences.zh: 还是他们全都支持联邦？

sentences.en: Or are they all for the Union?
sentences.zh: 真实情况到底是怎样的？

sentences.zh: 不管今天的那些新邦联主义者愿意怎么想象，他们其实并不支持邦联。

sentences.en: They don't support the Confederacy, whatever sort of neo-Confederates today might like to imagine.
sentences.zh: 从1861年战争爆发的那一刻起，基本上发生的是一场低烈度的奴隶起义。

sentences.en: What's happening essentially is that there is a low-level slave rebellion going on from the moment the war begins in 1861.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的黑人自我解放，将自由掌握在自己手中。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of black people self-emancipate, take freedom into their own hands.
sentences.zh: 而他们的焦点通常是联邦军队。

sentences.en: And the focus is often Union armies.
sentences.zh: 这也是迫使解放政策进入政治议程的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: And this is what forces, one of the main things that forces emancipation onto the political agenda.
sentences.zh: 所以在战争刚爆发的1861年春季，

sentences.en: So immediately, the very beginning of the war in spring 1861,
sentences.zh: 当成百上千人在弗吉尼亚或其他地方法律地位仍被视作财产的人涌来时，联邦指挥官们必须决定该怎么做。

sentences.en: Union commanders have to decide what to do when hundreds or thousands of people whose legal status in Virginia or wherever they are is as property.
sentences.zh: 当他们在联邦防线内寻求庇护时，指挥官们该如何应对？

sentences.en: What do they do when they essentially seek asylum in Union lines?
sentences.zh: 在战争初期，一些联邦指挥官把他们交还给了主人。

sentences.en: And some Union commanders in the early stages of the war return them to their masters.
sentences.zh: 许多人则另有对策——这是联邦将军本杰明·巴特勒耍的一个著名的花招，他把这些人称为“战争违禁品”。

sentences.en: Many of them say, and this is a kind of famous sleight of hand by a Union general, Benjamin Butler, who calls them contraband of war.
sentences.zh: 所以他把南方人声称这些人是财产的论点反过来对付他们，并说道：如果我抓住了你们的马匹或者武器，我当然

sentences.en: So he turns the argument of the South that these people are property against them and says, well, if I got hold of your horses or if I got hold of your armaments, I would,
sentences.zh: 会把它们作为战争违禁品没收。

sentences.en: of course, confiscate them as contraband of war.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这些人正如你们所说，是你们的财产，那么我将同样把他们作为战争违禁品扣押。

sentences.en: So if these people are, as you say, your property, then I'm going to seize them as contraband of war at all in the same way.
sentences.zh: 因此，“违禁品”这个词后来被广泛使用，用来统称那些自我解放和曾经被奴役的人。

sentences.en: And so that term contraband then comes into general usage as a general descriptor of essentially self-emancipated and formerly enslaved people.
sentences.zh: 那么那些著名的种植园，想必需要大量的人力来维持那套压迫机器的运转。

sentences.en: So the famous plantations, presumably it had required a large amount of manpower to keep the apparatus of oppression in place.
sentences.zh: 但这些人现在都去参加内战了。

sentences.en: But these guys are now going off to fight in the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 那么是谁在阻止奴隶们逃往北方呢？

sentences.en: So who is stopping the slaves from going to the North?
sentences.zh: 比以前少得多的人。

sentences.en: Many fewer people than before.
sentences.zh: 因此，你知道的，被奴役者逃跑的比率才会高得多。

sentences.en: Hence the much, you know, the higher rate of enslaved people running away.
sentences.zh: 而邦联在他们最初……

sentences.en: And the Confederacy, when they firSt...
sentences.zh: 他们在逃跑，但他们会袭击种植园吗？

sentences.en: They're running away, but are they attacking the plantations?
sentences.zh: 他们会把种植园烧毁之类的吗？

sentences.en: Are they kind of burning them down or...
sentences.zh: 是的，他们在某些情况下确实这么做了。

sentences.en: Yes, they are in some instances.
sentences.zh: 他们在某些情况下确实如此。

sentences.en: They are in some instances.
sentences.zh: 确实存在针对奴隶主的暴力事件。

sentences.en: There are instances of violence against enslavers.
sentences.zh: 存在这种情况……

sentences.en: There are...
sentences.zh: 邦联在引入征兵制时，

sentences.en: The Confederacy, when it introduces conscription,
sentences.zh: 出台了一条规则，试图通过规定来防止这种情况：如果你拥有的种植园里被奴役人数超过了一定数量，

sentences.en: introduces a rule that tries to prevent this by saying that if you have a plantation with more than a certain number of enslaved people,
sentences.zh: 你就可以免服兵役。

sentences.en: then you're allowed an exemption from conscription.
sentences.zh: 但随着战争的进行，这条规则也承受了压力。

sentences.en: But as the war goes on, that too comes under pressure.
sentences.zh: 所以它越来越难以维持。

sentences.en: So it's harder and harder to sustain.
sentences.zh: 因此这演变成了……

sentences.en: So it becomes...
sentences.zh: 奴隶制成了邦联最大的阿喀琉斯之踵。

sentences.en: Slavery becomes the big Achilles heel of the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 要在平时维持一个压迫性的奴隶制系统本来就很艰难。

sentences.en: It's really hard to maintain a system of oppressive slavery in the first place.
sentences.zh: 当你在自己的国土上进行一场战争时，要做到这一点就更难了。

sentences.en: It's even harder to do it when you're trying to fight a war on your own soil.
sentences.zh: 最后，局势变得如此糟糕，以至于李将军实际上向罗伯逊·戴维斯建议，他们应该像联邦那样武装奴隶。

sentences.en: And in the end, the situation gets so bad that Lee actually suggests to Robertson Davis that they should arm slaves, as the Union does.
sentences.zh: 在邦联行将就木的最后日子里，当时兵败如山倒的迹象不仅写在墙上，更写在他们每个人的脸上和所有的建筑上。

sentences.en: In the very dying days of the Confederacy, when the writing is not just on the wall, but it's all over their faces and all over the buildings.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像是希特勒武装13岁儿童的那种水平。

sentences.en: This is kind of Hitler-arming 13-year-olds kind of level.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 在最后关头，他们终于通过了一项法案，承诺向为邦联军队作战的被奴役者提供解放，但该法案从未付诸实施。

sentences.en: At the very dying days, they eventually pass a bill which could have promised emancipation to enslave people who fight for the Confederate Army, but it never goes into effect.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，亚当，在这个时候，他们实际上是在讨论为了维护某种身份认同而牺牲奴隶制。

sentences.en: What's interesting there, Adam, is that at that point, they're actually talking about sacrificing slavery to preserve their sort of sexual identity.
sentences.zh: 独立。

sentences.en: Independence.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们的独立。

sentences.en: Yeah, their independence.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的国家认同不仅仅是奴隶制的遮羞布。

sentences.en: So their national identity is not just a figly for slavery.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是有意义的。

sentences.en: It means something to them.
sentences.zh: 他们愿意为此放弃奴隶制？

sentences.en: And they would give up slavery for it?
sentences.zh: 这不可能吧……

sentences.en: That can't be...
sentences.zh: 对，但如果这真的是一场以这种格莱斯顿式的浪漫主义方式争夺民族自决权的斗争，那么他们肯定早就做出这种立场了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but if it had really been a fight for national self-determination in this Gladstonian romantic way, then they surely would have made, come to that position a good deal of it.
sentences.zh: 对，那我们能走到那个结局吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so could we come to that end?
sentences.zh: 所以林肯赢得选举，这真的成了棺材板上的最后一颗钉子。

sentences.en: So Lincoln wins election, and that really is the kind of the final nail in the coffin.
sentences.zh: 最终的结局是什么？

sentences.en: What is the end game?
sentences.zh: 最终的结局是，李将军的军队最终被迫在弗吉尼亚州西南部的阿波马托克斯法院投降，这被视为——

sentences.en: The end game is that Lee's army has eventually forced to surrender at Appomattox Courthouse in southwest Virginia, and that is taken,
sentences.zh: 尽管战场上仍然有邦联军队，但由于李将军的军队与邦联联系太紧密了，

sentences.en: although there are still Confederate armies in the field, because Lee's army has been so associated with the Confederacy,
sentences.zh: 而且李将军本人与邦联的形象也太密不可分了。

sentences.en: and the figure of Lee himself is so associated with the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 比起总统杰斐逊·戴维斯，他更能化身为邦联的象征，因此当李将军投降时，几乎所有人都认为这意味着战争的结束。

sentences.en: He personifies the Confederacy far more than Jefferson Davis, the president, does, that when Lee surrenders, that is regarded by virtually everybody as the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 关于那次投降，我只想快速问一个问题，因为投降的那个时刻非常重要，也就是阿波马托克斯法院。

sentences.en: And just one quick question about that, that surrender, because that surrender moment is very important, Appomattox Courthouse.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈论过圆颅党和骑士党的事情。

sentences.zh: 尤利西斯·S·

sentences.zh: 格兰特吧。

sentences.zh: 我对他的了解其实很少。

sentences.en: He's a sort of failure of a man, isn't he, Adam?
sentences.zh: 他算是个挺失败的男人，对吧，亚当？

sentences.en: He's a drunk.
sentences.zh: 他是个酒鬼。

sentences.en: Who is sort of transformed by the war.
sentences.zh: 却在战争中完成了一种蜕变。

sentences.en: He's Jared Harris in the film.
sentences.zh: 他在电影里由杰瑞德·哈里斯饰演。

sentences.en: He's transformed by the war, and he becomes this Lincoln's indispensable general.
sentences.zh: 他经历战争完成了蜕变，成为了林肯不可或缺的将军。

sentences.en: And the reason that he lingers in the memory, I mean, he tarnishes his own reputation because he becomes a sort of slightly shop-soiled president later on, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他之所以能在记忆中挥之不去——我是说，他后来因为当总统时名誉受损，变得有点像过期的商品，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's gilded age and corrupt and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他处在镀金时代，贪腐成风，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think he gets a bit of a bad rap, actually.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得其实他有点被冤枉了。

sentences.en: Very, Dan Jackson, friend of the show, very keen on him because he goes to Newcastle and Sunderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的老朋友丹·杰克逊非常崇拜他，因为他去过纽卡斯尔和桑德兰。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does in his global tour.

sentences.en: But anyway, sorry.
sentences.zh: 不过总之，抱歉。

sentences.zh: 但说到他和李的对比，他是个圆头圆脑、衣着寒酸的人物，而他接受了李的投降，李可是特意为此精心打扮了一番，对吧？

sentences.en: But Grant allows Lee and his men to leave with honour, and they get to keep their horses, and they get to go off, and he gives them rations.
sentences.zh: 但格兰特允许李和他的部下有尊严地离开，他们保住了自己的马匹，可以动身离开，他还发给他们给养。

sentences.en: Now, there are two ways of talking about that moment.
sentences.zh: 现在，看待那个时刻有两种方式。

sentences.en: I mean, we'll get into the legacy of the war in the next episode, but one is to say, oh, isn't that lovely?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们会在下一集探讨战争的遗产，但一种观点会说，哦，这不是很美好吗？

sentences.en: They're all friends again, and the union is remade and all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 大家又成了朋友，联邦重修旧好，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But, Adam, could you say, and I would say,
sentences.zh: 但是，亚当，你会不会说——而我会说——

sentences.en: that creates huge problems for the future because what it does is it almost recognises – instead of treating the Confederates as rebels and as traitors,
sentences.zh: 这为未来埋下了巨大的隐患，因为这样做几乎等于承认——没有把邦联人当作叛军和叛徒对待，

sentences.en: it recognises them as worthy, noble opponents.
sentences.zh: 而是承认他们是值得尊敬的、高尚的对手。

sentences.en: And in that moment at Appomattox Courthouse, you have the creation of this myth, the thing we've talked about so much, the cavalier idea.
sentences.zh: 于是在阿波马托克斯法院的那个瞬间，诞生了我们谈论过无数次的那个神话，即骑士精神的观念。

sentences.en: Oh, the Confederates were great, noble fellows, and it's such a shame they fell out.
sentences.zh: 哦，邦联人都是伟大、高尚的家伙，他们闹翻真是太可惜了。
